scope: Real internal reviewed-plan coordinator, with fresh-process local resume and completion; public SQL update/resume commands remain blocked.
workflow: Public offline init and online create/no-op produce one managed input, strict SQL runner and metadata-only downstream application.

Worker execute edits the actual project SQL predicate from 100 to 200, compiles the full project, saves and reloads a genuine reviewed format-6 file, then invokes the internal coordinator under a real local state lock.
The real Docker create succeeds once, then its acknowledgement is deliberately lost. The coordinator persists the interruption; the worker exits normally and releases its lock.
A fresh worker reloads the same on-disk project, original reviewed file and protected state, authorizes the exact durable operation and starts only the existing candidate.

After the completion audit and ownership postimage are written, a second injected error prevents control clear. A third fresh worker validates and clears the terminal operation without provider, ownership, authorization or audit rewrites.
Read-committed verification produces three records once, checks exact keys/values and committed offset 5 to 8, then public plan/apply returns to no-op with provider/state/audit snapshots unchanged.

cohort.module_tree_encoding: SHA256 of JSON module-relative-path to SHA256 map; sorted keys, compact separators.

limitations: This exercises the internal coordinator and typed local backend, not public CLI update/resume activation.

Three separate OS processes acquire fresh local locks, but both failures are injected at controlled boundaries and workers exit normally; this is not SIGKILL, power loss, Docker daemon loss or disk corruption.
The Kafka fixture is one owned broker with one input/output partition and PLAINTEXT; it does not establish multi-broker, authenticated TLS/SASL or distributed PostgreSQL-coordinator behavior.
The second interruption is before control clear, after its audit and ownership write, not an uncertain acknowledged clear response.
Raw exit code 143 is retained only after the strict observer validates clean closure and inactive-group retained offsets; exit code alone is not success.

The final public apply may regenerate ordinary local compilation/control files; assertions establish no provider change, unchanged ownership/state observation and unchanged incident/completion archive.
exactly_once_v2 is the configured Kafka processing mode, not a universal lifecycle or external-side-effect guarantee.
Local raw artifact paths are retained on this machine; committed digests identify them, but do not make those temporary artifacts portable.
Historical verification JSON files are unchanged and retain their original narrower source cohorts and limitations.
